newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opposition accuses army of holding peasants.
newsitem.headline: Mexico opposition accuses army of holding peasants.

text.p: Military troops in the southwestern state of Guerrero are holding four peasant farmers on the suspicion they are members of a guerrilla group, an opposition politician said on Friday.

An official with the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) claimed that soldiers had tortured the detainees to make them declare they were rebel members of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR).
Octaviano Santiago said the military operation took place on Thursday in the mountain town of Cuacoyulichan, 65 miles (110 km) from Acapulco.
He said the soldiers called residents to a meeting in the town's basketball court and read out a list of names, and then took the PRD party militants into custody.
"They took them and tortured them and said that they had to say they were members of the EPR," Santiago said.
Renewed fighting between Marxist guerrillas and the Mexican army in a poor southwestern state have sparked accusations of a dirty war this week.
Army troops and rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) have fought several times in the past few days in Guerrero state -- their first clashes this year.
The army said on Thursday at least nine soldiers and rebels were killed in the fighting. The rebels claim at least 60 people have been killed or wounded.
